body:
OBJECTIVES
- Students draw points, lines, line segments, rays, right, acute and obtuse angles, and perpendicular and parallel lines, and identify them in shapes (4.G.A.1).
- Students recognize angles as geometric shapes formed by two rays with a common endpoint and understand angle measurement in degrees as a fraction of a circle (4.MD.C.5).
- Students measure and sketch angles in whole-number degrees with a protractor (4.MD.C.6).
- Students recognize angle measure as additive and solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles, writing an equation with a symbol for the unknown (4.MD.C.7).
- Students classify two-dimensional figures by parallel or perpendicular lines and angles, including right triangles (4.G.A.2), and identify lines of symmetry (4.G.A.3).

MATERIALS
- Protractors, rulers and sharp pencils
- Paper circles and paper plates for folding into fractions of a turn
- Shape cards (squares, rectangles, rhombuses, trapezoids, parallelograms, kites, triangles) and capital letter cards
- Small mirrors or tracing paper for checking symmetry

FIVE-DAY PLAN
Day 1: Read The Geometry Around Us. Geometry hunt around the room: find segments, right angles, parallel and perpendicular lines. Lesson: Points, Lines, Rays and Angles.
Day 2: Fold a paper circle into halves, quarters and eighths to see 180, 90 and 45 degrees. Model the protractor: line up the center point and baseline, then read the row that starts at 0. Start Measuring and Adding Angles.
Day 3: Additive angles with paper wedges: put a 35-degree wedge and a 55-degree wedge together to make a right angle. Finish Measuring and Adding Angles.
Day 4: Shape sort with cards by parallel sides, perpendicular sides and right angles. Fold letters and shapes to find lines of symmetry. Assignment: Sorting Shapes and Finding Symmetry.
Day 5: Assessment: Geometry Check. Protractors and rulers are allowed.

DIFFERENTIATION
- Support: give pre-drawn angles to measure before asking students to draw their own; mark the 0 on the correct row of the protractor with a sticker.
- Support: use the corner of a sheet of paper as a right-angle checker.
- Stretch: find the angle between the hands of a clock at 2:00, 4:00 and 5:00, and explain the pattern (each hour is 30 degrees).
- Multilingual learners: build a picture glossary for ray, segment, parallel, perpendicular, acute, obtuse and symmetry, and use gestures (arms parallel, arms perpendicular) as a whole class.

FAMILY NOTE (send home at the start of the unit)
We are studying angles, lines and shapes. Your child is learning words like acute (less than a right angle), obtuse (more than a right angle), parallel (never meeting) and perpendicular (meeting at a right angle), and how to measure angles with a protractor. Go on a geometry hunt at home or on a walk: how many right angles can you find? Which letters on a street sign have a line of symmetry?
title: Teacher guide: Angles, Lines and Shapes
